title: Embeddings evaluation playbook — multilingual search + clustering sanity checks
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for onboarding new embedding models into the applied-ML evaluation suite. Focused on three evaluation slices: semantic search relevance (English + multilingual), clustering sanity checks (top-level class separation + noise sensitivity), and lightweight regression reporting to catch quality drifts during rollouts.

Context / motivation:
- We onboard >3 community/open embeddings per quarter; need consistent pass/fail criteria for product teams (Console, Hosted API, Dedicated).
- Must capture both retrieval utility (search) and structure preservation (clustering) across languages.
- Aim for tests that are fast (minutes — can run in CI), and also a longer nightly job that computes heavier metrics.

Datasets (quick inventory):
- en-ms-marco-mini: 10k curated queries + 100k doc corpus subset (semantic search dev set, English).
- multi-retrieval-2k: 2k queries, each translated to es, fr, de, zh (human-reviewed subset of seed queries).
- wiki-cluster-1k: 1k short Wikipedia paragraphs mapped to 50 coarse clusters (used for clustering sanity).
- product-faq-2k: customer-facing FAQ pairs (semantic similarity / duplicate detection).
- noise-probe-500: synthetic near-duplicates / adversarial paraphrases for stability checks.

Notes: most datasets are stored as CSV in s3://redwood-evals/embeddings/*. For CI we sample smaller shards (1k queries / 5k docs).

Evaluation protocol (high-level):
1) Preprocessing: normalize whitespace, remove punctuation-only tokens, lowercase for languages where safe (configurable per dataset).
2) Embedding generation: run model with default pooling (CLS or mean depending on model). Record model config: quantization, sequence length, pooling, normalization.
3) Semantic search evaluation: compute retrieval metrics for each query against corpus.
   - Primary metrics: Recall@10, mAP@10, nDCG@10.
   - Secondary: MRR@100, median rank.
   - Failure cases to log: anchor queries where golden answer not in top 100.
4) Clustering sanity checks: cluster embeddings (kmeans with k = ground truth clusters, and k = 2 * ground truth) and compute:
   - Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)
   - Normalized Mutual Information (NMI)
   - Silhouette score (for both cosine and euclidean)
   - Intra-cluster / inter-cluster distance ratio
5) Multilingual pass: for multi-retrieval-2k run retrieval per-language and then cross-lingual retrieval (query in en, documents in target lang). Compare per-lang delta vs English baseline.
6) Robustness checks: add noise-probe paraphrases and check similarity ordering stability (spearman correlation of similarity scores).
7) Regression gating: compare to baseline embedding version (pinned model) on a small subset. Flag if any critical metric drops >5% absolute or >10% relative (tunable).

Baselines and reference models:
- redwood-embed-base-v1 (internal baseline)
- open-embed-compact (community reference)
- tiny-benchmark (fast cheap baseline for smoke tests)

Example metric acceptance criteria (suggested, not final):
- English semantic search: Recall@10 >= 0.78, nDCG@10 >= 0.52
- Multilingual: per-lang delta (vs English) no worse than -0.12 relative for nDCG@10 on major langs (es, fr, de). For zh allow -0.18 initially.
- Clustering: ARI >= 0.46 on wiki-cluster-1k, silhouette(cosine) >= 0.12
- Robustness: spearman(similarity scores) >= 0.85 for near-duplicate probes

Quick sample prompts / similarity pairs (for prompt-guided embedding models):
- Query: "How do I reset my password?"
  Positive doc: "Steps to reset forgotten passwords via settings -> security."
  Negative doc: "How to change username display"
- Paraphrase pair: "Cancel my subscription" vs "I want to stop my paid plan" (expect high similarity)
- Cross-lingual example: EN query "data retention policy" -> FR doc "politique de conservation des données" (should rank high)

Regression report template (CI-friendly):
- header: model_name, model_id, embedding_dim, pooling, quantization, dataset_shard_id
- rows: metric_name, baseline_value, new_value, delta_abs, delta_pct, pass/fail, notes
- attach top-10 failing queries per dataset (short CSV) and 5 example clusters with membership lists

Operational notes / CI integration:
- Fast smoke test: run on sample shards (100 q x 1k docs) — target < 3 minutes per model on 8 A100 vCPU job.
- Nightly full suite: larger shards + clustering; scheduled on dedicated GPU pool.
- Store artifacts in s3 with path: s3://redwood-evals/embeddings/<model_name>/<date>/report.json (keep 90 days).
- Visual diffs: quick scatterplot of PCA(2) vs UMAP(2) stored as small PNGs for human inspection.

Known open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide final acceptance thresholds by running the suite on last 6 public models and setting percentile cutoffs (ask product for tolerances).
- Add language-specific normalization recipes (e.g., aggressive romanization for CJK? probably not).
- Evaluate behavior for long documents (>1k tokens) and if chunking strategy impacts ranking — need a separate test.
- Formalize storage format for per-query debug traces (should include tokenization + kv-cache footprints for advanced debugging).

Quick checklist for onboarding a new model (engineer workflow):
- [ ] Add model config to models.yml (embedding type, pooling, max_len, normalization)
- [ ] Run fast smoke test -> must pass basic sanity (no runtime errors, dims match)
- [ ] Run semantic search shard + clustering shard locally, inspect top failures
- [ ] Push nightly run request (tagging evaluation team)
- [ ] Draft regression report; if gated failure, open ML-EVAL ticket and cc product/security

Appendix: lightweight result snapshot example (CSV-ish text for human review):
model,metric,dataset,baseline,new,delta_abs,delta_pct,pass
redwood-embed-base-v1,Recall@10,en-ms-marco-mini,0.80,0.79,-0.01,-1.25,true
redwood-embed-base-v1,nDCG@10,multi-retrieval-2k-en,0.54,0.50,-0.04,-7.4,false
open-embed-compact,ARI,wiki-cluster-1k,0.49,0.45,-0.04,-8.2,false

Contact / reviewers: Marco (embeddings infra), Evelyn (multilingual), Samir (search UX).

Last notes: keep this doc intentionally informal — it's the playbook for rapid iteration. When we land thresholds and canonical datasets, we will extract a "formal spec" into Confluence but keep links here for experiments and ad-hoc runs.

-- Aisha
